title: fleet-work event v1
description: ONE EVENT IN THE FLEET-WORK RECORD: one flat JSON object on one line of <HORDE_HOME>/metrics/fleet-work/events.jsonl. Read by core/FleetWork.ps1 and appended only by core/FleetWorkStore.ps1, behind the metrics consent gate; nothing in Horde sends it anywhere. THE LINE: schemaVersion, kind, lane, id, time, values. kind is a closed list; values is a map whose fields are fixed by the kind, each in its own definition below (<kind>Values), which core/FleetWork.ps1 checks the values against: the subset of draft-07 that core/Schema.ps1 implements has no oneOf or if, so the choice by kind is made there. THE ID is set once by whoever writes the event, before its first attempt, and kept on every retry: a second write of an id already in the file is answered 'exists' and adds no line. A LINE IS NEVER CHANGED OR REMOVED. Whatever ends or reverses an earlier line is a NEW line of its own kind whose values name the earlier line's id: a wait-end's values.ends is the id of the wait it ends. A status line replaces nothing either: the current status of a lane is its last status line in the file. Every text is bounded by its pattern (the subset has no maxLength) and is one line with no control character. What the schema cannot say is checked in core/FleetWork.ps1: that a time is a date that exists, that a wait does not start after it was written, that an end does not name itself, and that no text holds anything shaped like a conversation, a credential or customer data.

kind.description: wait: a session starts waiting on someone or something. wait-end: a wait ends, and what ended it. status: a lane's status record as its orchestrator last wrote it.

lane.description: The lane the event belongs to, in the plain words its orchestrator always uses for it.

id.description: 8 to 64 characters, lower case, set once by the writer of the event and kept on every retry. core/FleetWorkStore.ps1's New-HordeFleetWorkEventId gives 32 lower-case hex digits.

time.description: When the event was written, in UTC.

values.description: The fields of this kind: the definition <kind>Values.

label.description: A lane's or a session's name: letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores, 1 to 64 characters.

utc.description: A UTC time, to the minute, the second or the millisecond.

line120.description: One line of 1 to 120 characters, with no control character. The line in the file is ASCII; a character beyond it is a \u escape there, and counts here as one character.

waitingOn.description: Who or what it waits on, a closed list: the owner who decides, the orchestrator above it, another lane, a device, an outside service. Not 'nothing': a session that waits on nothing has no open wait.

waitingOnName.description: Optional. Which one, when there are several: the lane's name, the device's label.

since.description: When the wait began. Never after the line's time.

endsWhen.description: What would end the wait, in plain words.

ends.description: The id of the wait line this line ends. The end time is this line's time.

unblockedBy.description: What ended the wait, in plain words.

session.description: The orchestrator that wrote the status.

doing.description: What it is doing now. At most 120 characters.

finished.description: The last thing it finished. At most 120 characters.

blocked.description: 'no', or one sentence saying what stops all its useful work.

x-horde-file.name: events.jsonl
x-horde-file.encoding: ASCII; one event per line, each line ended by a single LF; any other character is written as a \u escape
x-horde-file.readers: core/FleetWork.ps1 (Read-HordeFleetWorkEventText for one line, Read-HordeFleetWorkLog for the file's text)
x-horde-file.writers: core/FleetWorkStore.ps1 (Save-HordeFleetWorkEvent), which only appends, never changes or removes a line, and sends nothing anywhere
